precepts.text: Receive with meekness the engrafted word, the law and the testimony, which is able to save your soul, and be ye doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves like the man who forgets his face in the glass and goes back to sin. Whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty and continueth, a doer of the work, shall be blessed in his deed.
precepts.point: The same Paul who said no man is justified by the works of the law says not the hearers of the law are just before God but the doers of the law shall be justified. Was he schizophrenic? No; the law in Galatians is sacrifice, elaborated in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, and the law here is the commandments, and faith comes first and the works follow.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
In Galatians Paul says you are not justified by the works of the law, and Christians say, see, we don’t have to keep the commandments; Christ died for us, just believe. Then the same Paul writes, “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” Was Paul schizophrenic? No. The law in Galatians is animal sacrifice, explained in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, which Christ did away with. The law here is the commandments. Faith comes first, and then the works follow.

Christ’s brother James answers the same way: “Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”: lay aside all sin. “And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The engrafted word is the law and the testimony. Some heard in church that the law cannot save you, only Christ can. The law in Christ saves you; keeping God’s commandments can save your soul.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” That takes you right back to Romans 2:13. Christianity tells you that you do not have to keep God’s commandments and will still be saved; they deceive themselves and others. “For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” He reads the Bible, says yeah okay, and goes back to sinning, looking in the mirror and forgetting what he saw.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.” The work is the commandments; blessed in his deed is justified. Christ gave us liberty from the law of sin and death, the sacrifices under which a man “died without mercy”, but that liberty is not freedom from doing the commandments. The doers of the law shall be justified.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: that is the word, the engrafted word.
precepts.point: The same Paul who said no man is justified by the works of the law says not the hearers of the law are just before God but the doers of the law shall be justified. Was he schizophrenic? No; the law in Galatians is sacrifice, elaborated in Hebrews 7, 9 and 10, and the law here is the commandments, and faith comes first and the works follow.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
James says, “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” What is the engrafted word? Isaiah answers it: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

The law and the testimony is the word. So the word James says is able to save your soul, the word we must be doers of and not hearers only, is the law and the testimony: the commandments of God.

That is why Paul could say, “not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.” The law he means there is the commandments, the engrafted word, not the sacrifices that Christ did away with.

So when the church says the law cannot save you, they are not speaking according to this word. Those who speak not according to the law and the testimony have no light in them. The word saves, Christ saves, and the doer of the word is the one justified.

precepts.text: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law. Romans 7:1: I speak to them that know the law. Paul is writing to Jews, with northern kingdom in the congregations, but all of them saints.
precepts.point: Beware lest ye, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own steadfastness. The error comes from those who stumble at the other scriptures, the Old Testament. When you teach your oppressor can receive the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you are in the error of the wicked.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

precepts.text: God will render to every man according to his deeds, to the Jew first and also to the Gentile: for there is no respect of persons with God.
precepts.point: Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.
precepts.why:
Respect unto his chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons. God “will render to every man according to his deeds: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath”.

“Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile”: the Jew is the southern kingdom, and the Gentile is the northern kingdom that was Hellenized. Both get tribulation and anguish for evil. “But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: For there is no respect of persons with God.”

The nation is chosen above the nations, and God has respect unto that nation; but inside the nation every man is rendered to according to his deeds.

precepts.text: Circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law; he is a Jew, which is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart; it speaks to lawbreaking, not to ending the covenant of the flesh.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. “For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.” The Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision.

“Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?” The uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised.

“he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter”. This speaks to lawbreaking, not to ending the covenant of the flesh. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say; the covenant that the Lord sought to kill Moses over still stands.

precepts.text: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes; there go the synonyms, foolish and babes and youth, so we must come back as a baby knowing we do not know anything.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.” There go the synonyms again: foolish and babes, like the simple and the youth void of understanding.

The form of knowledge and of the truth is in the law, and it is taught to the foolish and to babes. So we must come back as a baby, knowing we do not know anything, and let the sure testimony of the Lord make the simple wise.

precepts.text: Tribulation and wrath upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, for there is no respect of persons with the Most High.
precepts.point: Peter opens his mouth and says the Most High is no respecter of persons, but in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted, and the word was sent unto the children of Israel. "No respecter of persons" does not mean nations are equal, because the Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people; it means he does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law, so whether a man sins outside the law or inside it he is judged.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile; But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: For there is no respect of persons with God.”

No respect of persons means judgment by the law: evil is repaid and good is rewarded, whoever does it. And it says the Jew first, and also the Gentile, because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin and Levi to rise up first. The Gentiles are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
This is a very famous scripture used by Christians to argue against keeping the law, but Paul is making reference to a specific law. Romans settles that we are justified by keeping the commandments: “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.”

The doers of the law shall be justified. So “the works of the law” by which no flesh is justified cannot be the commandments; it is a different law.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The law whose doers are justified is the commandments, as Romans 2 goes on to show. “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”, confident of being “a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness.” Then: “thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal? Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?”

Do not steal, do not commit adultery, abhor idols: those are the commandments, and the doers of that law shall be justified. So we ARE justified by keeping the commandments, and the works of the law in Galatians 2:16 refer to a different law.
